trust_decision.summary: Which classes may be instantiated and field-populated by zero-config (reflective) Compact deserialization. The client controls the schema typeName, so the decision must be a class filter (built-in JDK blocklist + default internal blocklist + configured blocklist/allowlist, with a defaults-disabled switch) consulted before a registration or reflective serializer exists, inside CompactStreamSerializer; reads of now-ineligible data degrade to GenericRecord instead of failing.

landing_point.why: The only path from attacker-supplied bytes to an arbitrary class: read() takes schema.getTypeName() straight off the wire and resolves it to a class (getOrCreateRegistration0 at :246-262), then the reflective serializer instantiates it and sets its fields. Someone reading 'low-privileged client gets arbitrary member memory access' greps the compact package for typeName-to-class resolution here; the only pre-existing 'blocklist' reference sits one file away in ReflectiveCompactSerializer.createFastReadWriteCaches (ReflectiveCompactSerializer.java:181-186), which is where a narrow reader stops.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about member-side deserialization, so the config layer can be argued to be plumbing: the programmatic API (CompactSerializationConfig.setZeroConfigFilter) is enough to configure the filter, and the XML/YAML/Spring parsers and the config XML generator merely mirror the existing java-serialization-filter support; a solver can add that the config copy constructor and equals/hashCode are bookkeeping that 'cannot affect the runtime check'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reading already-stored compact data whose class is now restricted must degrade to a GenericRecord (rolling upgrade, mixed restricted and unrestricted clients/members) instead of throwing; an over-broad fix that rejects the class on read breaks existing map data and mixed clusters. Separately, explicitly registered CompactSerializers must keep overriding the filter for any class (ValueReaderWriters.java:213-219).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: nested compact read (getObject, and getObjectFromArray/getArrayOfObject at :781-784,:1074-1076) that resolves a class from the nested schema typeName through serializer.read
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Nested reads are a distinct call site in another class; a maintainer fixing the top-level read would plausibly wire the same restriction here separately, which is why the real fix needed the exception-rewind behaviour.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: array-of-compact element reader/writer that passes the component class into readArrayOfCompact
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The existing code already has separate field-type and component-type verification branches (:213-219 vs :235-241), so a sibling element-class rule is a natural addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: config copy constructor / merge route that must carry the new filter (and the null-unsafe JavaSerializationFilterConfig copy constructor at JavaSerializationFilterConfig.java:31-35)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Hazelcast copies Config/ClientConfig through these copy constructors; dropping the new field silently removes an operator's restriction, and the copy constructor NPEs when only a blacklist is set.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: config save route emitting zero-config-filter, shared by member ConfigXmlGenerator.java:539 and client ClientConfigXmlGenerator.java:311
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A new compact sub-element must be emitted as well as parsed, and the shared helper gives the client generator a second call site for free.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second config parser implementation for Spring XML, in a different Maven module
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Spring config support duplicates the XML parsing rules by hand; the real fix had to touch this module and its own XSD.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: record serializer as a second serializer selected by getOrCreateRegistration before the reflective one
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The registration code picks javaRecordSerializer or reflectiveSerializer; a maintainer guarding only the reflective branch leaves the record branch open, and the pinned catch-all at :132-133 swallows the reason.

O9_family: Improper input validation (CWE-20) over a class identity taken from untrusted data, enabling unsafe object construction / untrusted-data deserialization (CWE-502-like) through reflection

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the existing JDK-prefix check in CompactUtil.canBeSerializedAsCompact / ReflectiveCompactSerializer.createFastReadWriteCaches with a com.hazelcast package blocklist and keep throwing on read; that keeps the instantiate-then-check order (ReflectiveCompactSerializer.java:151 vs :155) and re-breaks reads of already-stored data instead of falling back to GenericRecord.
